headline: Rooppur Nuclear Plant: Unit-1 begins first nuclear fission reaction
summary: The milestone marks the reactor's first criticality, bringing Bangladesh one step closer to generating nuclear electricity.
details: Unit-1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant initiated its first nuclear fission reaction on Monday afternoon, marking a major milestone for the country's first nuclear power project.

The reaction, which creates a self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction, began at approximately 3:34 PM after receiving regulatory approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA).
This development marks the reactor's first criticality, the point at which it reaches a stable critical state at minimum thermal power and sustains a nuclear chain reaction for the first time.
Project officials stated that engineers are closely monitoring reactor parameters, safety systems, and control equipment throughout the process.
The physical start-up phase, including first criticality, is expected to take about 30 to 40 days, after which power generation will be increased gradually based on test results.
According to BAERA Chairman Mahamudul Hasan, the plant received a B-2 commissioning licence last Thursday, authorizing the start of the fission reaction.

Dr. Md Zahedul Hassan, managing director of Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd, explained that heat produced through nuclear fission will convert water into high-pressure steam to drive turbines and produce electricity.
caption:
Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant has just hit a major milestone: Unit-1 has successfully started its first nuclear fission reaction.

Unit-1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant initiated its first nuclear fission reaction on Monday afternoon, marking a major milestone for the country's first nuclear power project.

The reaction, which creates a self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction, began at approximately 3:34 PM after receiving regulatory approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA).

This development marks the reactor's first criticality, the point at which it reaches a stable critical state at minimum thermal power and sustains a nuclear chain reaction for the first time.

Project officials stated that engineers are closely monitoring reactor parameters, safety systems, and control equipment throughout the process.

The physical start-up phase, including first criticality, is expected to take about 30 to 40 days, after which power generation will be increased gradually based on test results.

According to BAERA Chairman Mahamudul Hasan, the plant received a B-2 commissioning licence last Thursday, authorizing the start of the fission reaction.

Dr. Md Zahedul Hassan, managing director of Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd, explained that heat produced through nuclear fission will convert water into high-pressure steam to drive turbines and produce electricity.

headline_marked: Dengue crisis: [[Dengue death toll crosses 300]] as 2,193 hospitalised in 24 hours
headline: Dengue crisis: Dengue death toll crosses 300 as 2,193 hospitalised in 24 hours
summary: The DGHS reports a record single-day hospitalization figure as the national death toll rises to 303.
details: At least four dengue patients died and 2,193 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours until 8:00am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This marks the highest single-day hospitalization figure recorded so far.
Of the recent deaths, two were reported in the Khulna division, while one each occurred in the Chattogram and Rajshahi divisions.
With these latest figures, the total number of deaths has risen to 303 and the total number of cases has reached 99,275.
Currently, 6,069 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country.
